In the interest of providing as many options as possible to those who are interested in the Golden Dawn, I want to highlight the different Orders that exist today. The Open Source Order is based on the original Hermetic Order but was founded in 2002 by Sam Webster. He cited the principles of the open-source software movement as the driving force behind this particular Order, specifically:

The Open Source Order is founded on the principle that true spirituality is omnipresent and access to it cannot be owned or controlled by any group or individual. Sufficiently skilled practitioners can and do modify the practices to serve specific purposes or to take advantage of the century-plus development in the craft to improve their effect.

OSOGD integrates Thelema into its teachings and embraces Eastern philosophy and practices. Unfortunately, no on-line or distance training exists for magical aspirants and initiates must travel to the Lodge located in Northern California to join.

This is very appealing in that they recognize that no one magickal order can claim sole ownership of the magick rituals that the golden dawn uses, because these rituals merely tap into universal magickal laws, like the laws of nature. Nobody can own the universal lessons, especially since many of these are thousands of years old.

Universal Income guarantees a minimum level of income to replace all other forms of assistance. If its done, how would we react to a situation where we unintentionally create communities that grow in size, but remain poor?

Native American reservations do get a similar stipend, but it seems to hurt them more than help. What would prevent UI from turning more of America into a place where there is rampant rape, alcoholism, and poor health?
How do supporters of universal income deal with Native American reservations?
As a native American I don't see how this would hurt anything. If you could elaborate why this would be bad, that would help immensely.

The most common argument against universal income is that people would just throw the money away which in native american reservations and left leaning European nations this has been shown to not be true. While a few just throw the money away with poor decisions UI tends to be more positive than negative. With its implementation teen pregnancy rates decrease and abortion rates decrease because birth control becomes affordable. More people go into higher education and overtime more people are employed because a job is both socially and monetarily preferable to what is received from universal income along with helping people not become homeless which makes getting a job exponentially more difficult. Your view assumes the worst in people however I don't support UI for all of America as it is too vast and diverse economically and politically for universal income to be carried out well or at all.

Native American reservations do get a similar stipend

Not really. Native Americans get about $3,000 a year in cash assistance. All of that money immediately leaves the reservation in the form of consumable products. The stipend would have to be much greater for people to have some savings, and invest it into the community.

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reservation_poverty

Your claims regarding native american reservations need citation, because according to the New York Times, basic income helped the people at the Eastern Bend Cherokee Reservation in North Carolina. The main reason why Native Americans have problems is because of racism. On a per, capita basis, native americans are the most victimized group in America when it comes to hate crimes. They need more than money to fix that kind of problem.

Basic income has been advocated for by Martin Lutheer King, economists like Hayek and Freidman, liberals like senator McGovern and conservatives like Richard Nixon. The results of basic income in Alaska and various parts of India and Africa have been positive, causing a decrease in crime and improved nutrition. It also increases the velocity of money, which raises GDP.

If you are interested in how basic income would effect America, look at this paper about what happened when basic income was tried in Manitoba. They gave everybody a stipend from 1974 to 1979, and found that it resulted in the people being more healthy and better educated.

Reduce/eliminate population growth the same way that you do everywhere else. Make birth control easy to obtain, provide people with sex ed and opportunities to get an education that would benefit them and society as a whole.

Uh no. There is no similar stipend for native reservations.

http://tribaldirectory.com/tribal-enrollment-benefits/

In fact, take it on the word of the BIA

http://www.bia.gov/cs/groups/public/documents/text/idc002656.pdf

It's page 2. The funds that people do get (and most tribes don't), would be from settlements (very few), land use and resource use settlements (many of which had to be fought for in court for many many many many years), or from businesses that the tribe runs (which can hardly be considered a stipend. Really).

There are some tribes that get disbursements that are given out because of things like oil reserves and stuff, but for the most part that kind of thing doesn't exist. You don't really get dick for being Native most of the time (other than people asking to touch your hair, or asking you questions about nature. Ask me about your computer instead, probably get a better answer). Incidentally, cash assistance is something anyone poor can get. Half of my sister's friends are on it, and not a single one of them has a drop of native in em.

The issues with alcoholism, crime, and poor health are issues that happen with poverty, not simply with being native. You see them any place people are poor. It definitely doesn't help that for the most part the Native community is broken. We're so wrapped up in the idea of blood quantum most of us can't see anything else, including how racist it is. Casinos have been even worse, because a few tribes have ended up disenrolling large amounts of members just because they want greater payments, and using blood quantum as a basis. Creating more division in communities that badly need cohesion.

But I'm going off a bit in the wrong direction here, so let's get back on topic. You can't just throw money at people to deal with poverty, because they are going to spend it with that mindset. It's a fucked up mindset. You have to teach them how to spend, and save, and overcome the insidious little mental habits that screw you over when you are poor, and help ensure you stay that way. Things like needing to spend extra money right now, or the urge to overspend on gifts because you never were able to. Not knowing how to shop because you always just bought the cheap shit that's ready made and screws your health over because no one ever had any time between their like 3 minimum wage jobs to cook you anything, or teach you how. So that's just what you eat, because you had to. Not buying stuff that lasts, because you don't even understand the concept (I've literally had to explain to people that they should buy the 200$ pair of well made leather boots, rather than the 60$ shittily made poor quality pair, because if they take care of the well made pair they won't have to buy boots ever year, or ever again). How having credit, and having credit cards is a good thing. Not to mention how to use them properly. You also have to do it with tact, because the first thing thrown at you is gonna be "fuck you mr richguy, don't tell me how to live".

I'm kind of down for the idea of universal income tbh. Make it so people can aspire and earn more, but make it a comfortably livable basic minimum? Sounds great tbh.
